response.executive_summary: Stage10 cannot answer its stated goal. Six near-identical line logs plus a policy-complete answer prompt test instruction-following under planted faults, not whether metadata improves usefulness. The checker only rejects syntax it was built to reject; the metric cannot support even a scoped utility claim.
response.recommended_decision: Do not run as a usefulness study. Either add non-trivial help-cases, kind/token controls, and a pre-registered no-generalization rule, or relabel this a 6-fixture fault-injection probe and drop the metadata-utility question.
assumptions: One sample per cell on one model; extractor output is overwritten on 4/6 cases.
Source kind may be structured in metadata arms but only implicit in raw text.
Answer prompt already encodes the full A/B/none rule, so metadata is a shortcut or distractor, not new evidence.
Checker is exact-line, unique-declaration, parse-equals-value inside the sole [observed] block.
reasons: Usefulness is untested: every source is already a trivial key:value list. There is no hard-to-parse artifact where correct metadata could help. The design is biased toward neutral or harmful metadata.
Only clean_matching and wrong_winner have a justified choice. Four cells are none. That cannot measure improved usefulness.
Injected faults are rejected by construction (absent quote, value≠parse, non-unique line). This does not test wrong metadata that would pass the checker.
wrong_winner is the only cell that can show both block-vs-summary discipline and a metadata-induced miss of a justified A.
report_only tests fixture kind, not extraction or checking. If kind is not equally visible in the raw arm, conditions are not comparable.
Checked arm has extra tokens and a rejection channel the others lack; latency/tokens are unmatched, so no efficiency inference.

Correctness + unsupported endorsement + missed justified choice on predeclared fixtures only supports: did this model change answers under planted vs checked vs raw context. Not utility, mitigation in the wild, or production gating.
Prompt already says metadata is advisory and rejection ≠ absence. Compliance with that sentence is the real dependent variable.
risks: Checker edges: whitespace, colon spacing, case, field synonyms, two [observed] blocks (sole fails closed), multiline values, quote that is an exact line but the wrong field, winner treated like a scope field.
Model treats checked-unknown as proof the source lacks the field (explicitly warned; still the likely miss on wrong_winner and clean extraction).
Raw arm fails report_only from missing structured kind, inflating a false metadata benefit.
Candidate arm looks worse only because faults were planted after extraction, not because extractors are dangerous.
Citation substring checks will greenwash answers that quote the observed block and still pick the injected winner.
Any write-up that says metadata helps or checking mitigates will overclaim a smoke test.
disagreements: A defender can say the brief already disclaims authentication, entailment, holdout, and production, so a narrow probe is in-scope.
Six fixtures may be enough as a pre-live gate that the harness wires three arms and the checker rejects the four seeds.
Same prompt across arms is a real control; adding help-cases would confound format with metadata.
Checked-unknown leaving original text is the right non-repair policy even if models misuse it.
missing_information: Exact payload per arm: is kind, field set, and rejection reason serialized, and is raw given the same kind field?
Extractor schema, parse rule after colon, uniqueness/whitespace/case policy, behavior with 0 or 2 [observed] blocks.
Decoding settings, whether 18 calls are single-shot, and any seed.
A pre-registered analysis that forbids usefulness language unless help-cases exist.
At least one noisy source with correct metadata (help) and one syntactically valid but target-wrong field that passes the checker (checker blind spot).
How unsupported endorsement vs missed justified choice will be scored when explanation and recommendation conflict.
